representation_plans.learner_operation: Classify a case on generation and rank axes independently.
representation_plans.text_nonvisual_equivalent: Present a four-cell list crossing across-generation versus within-life with changed-rank versus similar-rank.

representation_plans.learner_operation: Compare a focal person’s position with a parent’s position.
representation_plans.text_nonvisual_equivalent: State the parent and child positions, time points, and relative rank without classifying the mobility.

representation_plans.learner_operation: Separate basic-needs sufficiency from position relative to social norms.
representation_plans.text_nonvisual_equivalent: List basic-needs access and society-relative participation indicators in separate labeled groups.

representation_plans.learner_operation: Trace segregation or isolation to reduced access and participation.
representation_plans.text_nonvisual_equivalent: State the separating condition, the blocked connection, and the resulting participation limit in sequence.

representation_plans.learner_operation: Sort measures into health outcomes versus health-care access or delivery.
representation_plans.text_nonvisual_equivalent: Present each measure with its group values and label whether it records health status or a care-system process.

representation_plans.learner_operation: Keep observed care-system differences and observed health outcomes in separate boxes.
representation_plans.text_nonvisual_equivalent: List the care-system observation and health-outcome observation separately without drawing a causal arrow.

representation_plans.learner_operation: Identify which group-patterned measure differs and classify its domain.
representation_plans.text_nonvisual_equivalent: State the groups, measure, units, and values in a table without interpreting causality.

demand_inventory.description: Distinguish intergenerational comparison from intragenerational change.
Distinguish vertical rank change from horizontal movement at a similar rank.
Identify a meritocracy claim and avoid treating the claim itself as proof of equal opportunity.
Identify absolute poverty from inability to secure basic necessities.
Identify relative poverty from resources below prevailing social standards despite basic survival.
Explain how segregation or isolation restricts resource access and social participation.
Classify disease, mortality, life expectancy, and other status differences as health disparities.
Classify access, utilization, wait time, coverage, or delivery differences as health-care disparities.
Identify class, gender, or race patterning while avoiding unsupported causal inference.

changed_task_decision_points.decision_point: The near task classifies a trajectory on time and rank axes; the changed task evaluates what a meritocracy statement claims. Reusing only the mobility label misses the shift from classification to claim evaluation.
near_trace: Identify whether the comparison is across generations or within one life.
Identify whether relative social rank changes or stays similar.
changed_trace: Locate the explanation offered for the mobility outcome.
Identify whether ability and effort are presented as the basis of reward.
Label the meritocracy invocation while checking whether equal opportunity is evidence or merely assumed.

changed_task_decision_points.decision_point: The near task classifies a resource condition as absolute or relative poverty; the changed task traces a segregation/isolation mechanism to blocked participation. Reusing the poverty label alone misses the access pathway.
near_trace: Identify whether basic necessities can be secured.
If they can, compare resources with prevailing social standards.
Classify absolute or relative poverty from the decisive comparison.
changed_trace: Identify the separating or isolating condition.
Identify which resource, network, or institution becomes harder to reach.
Explain the resulting restriction in participation as social exclusion.

changed_task_decision_points.decision_point: The near task classifies one outcome measure; the changed task separates a care-system measure from an outcome measure in the same case. Treating every difference as health status collapses the care/outcome boundary.
near_trace: Decide whether it is health status or a care-system process.
Classify the observed group difference without adding a cause.
changed_trace: Place appointment access or delivery in the health-care box and disease outcome in the health box.
Report both disparity types while withholding causal direction unless evidence supports it.
